title.zh: 卷四十二 列傳第二十三 王晏 蕭諶 蕭坦之 江祏
title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 23: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiangshi
title.raw: 卷四十二 列傳第二十三 王晏 蕭諶 蕭坦之 江祏 Volume 42 Biographies 23: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiangshi

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷四十二‧列傳第二十三

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23

sentences.zh: 王晏 蕭諶 蕭坦之 江祏

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiang Shi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, and Jiang Shi

sentences.zh: 王晏字士彥，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a man of Langya, Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a native of Linyi in Langya Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弘之，通直常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongzhi was a Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Hongzhi served as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 父普曜，祕書監。

translations.literal: His father Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晏，宋大明末起家臨賀王國常侍，員外郎，巴陵王征北板參軍，安成王撫軍板刑獄，隨府轉車騎。

translations.literal: Yan, at the end of the Song era of Daming, first entered service as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng, and followed the establishment when it became the Chariots and Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Liu Song Daming era, Yan began his career as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then served as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, and as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng; when that establishment became the Chariots and Cavalry staff, he transferred with it.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王燮爲郢州，晏爲安西主簿。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jinxing, Xie, was made governor of Ying Province, Yan was his western pacification chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xie of Jinxing was assigned to Ying Province, Yan served as his western pacification chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲長史，與晏相遇。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was chief administrator, and met Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wudi of Qi was chief administrator there, and he and Yan became acquainted.

sentences.zh: 府轉鎮西，板晏記室諮議。

translations.literal: When the establishment became western pacification, Yan was appointed on its board as recorder and adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the establishment was reorganized as the western pacification staff, Yan was appointed recorder and adviser on its board.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事難，鎮西職僚皆隨世祖鎮盆城，上時權勢雖重，而衆情猶有疑惑，晏便專心奉事，軍旅書翰皆委焉。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair brought crisis, the western pacification staff all followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng; though his power was already weighty, popular sentiment still harbored doubts, and Yan then devoted himself to service—military and documentary matters were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis of Shen Youzhi's rebellion, the western pacification staff followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng. Though his power was already formidable, many still hesitated; Yan devoted himself wholeheartedly to his service, and all military correspondence was placed in his hands.

sentences.zh: 性甚便僻，漸見親侍。

translations.literal: His nature was very adaptable and accommodating, and he gradually came to be treated with intimate attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and obliging by nature, and gradually won intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 乃留爲上征虜撫軍府板諮議，領記室。

translations.literal: He was then retained as a board adviser of the Heir Apparent's northern expedition and pacification army staff, concurrently heading the recorder's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was then kept on as a board adviser on the Heir Apparent's northern expedition and pacification army staff, concurrently heading the recorder's office.

sentences.zh: 從還都，遷領軍司馬，中軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital, he was transferred to be marshal of the Palace Guard, and an attendant gentleman of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: On their return to the capital, he was promoted to marshal of the Palace Guard and attendant gentleman of the central army.

sentences.zh: 常在上府，參議機密。

translations.literal: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, taking part in confidential deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, participating in confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 建元初，轉太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to be a junior mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 世祖在東宮，專斷朝事，多不聞啓，晏慮及罪，稱疾自疏。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace made sole decisions on court affairs and often did not report them; Yan feared he would be implicated in guilt and claimed illness to distance himself.
translations.idiomatic: While the Heir Apparent held court from the Eastern Palace, he often decided state affairs on his own without reporting them upward. Yan feared he would be held accountable and pleaded illness to keep his distance.

sentences.zh: 尋領射聲校尉，不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was made to head the Archers' Guard, but he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed colonel of the Archers' Guard but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，轉長兼侍中，意任如舊。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent took the throne, Yan was transferred to acting regular attendant-in-ordinary, with trust and appointment as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent ascended the throne, Yan was made acting regular attendant-in-ordinary, with the same trust and favor as before.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，領步兵校尉，遷侍中祭酒，校尉如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he headed the Footsoldiers Guard, was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, and retained his colonelcy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming, he was made colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard and promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, retaining his colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，起爲輔國將軍、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was recalled from mourning to be a general who assists the state and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, he was recalled from mourning to serve as General Who Assists the State and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 晏父普曜藉晏勢宦，多歷通官。

translations.literal: Yan's father Puyao, relying on Yan's power in office, passed through many high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's father Wang Puyao, relying on his son's influence, held a succession of high offices.

sentences.zh: 晏尋遷左衞將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: Yan was soon transferred to be General of the Left Guard and was given the additional title of supervisor of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was soon made General of the Left Guard with the additional title of supervisor of attendance.

sentences.zh: 未拜，而普曜卒，居喪有稱。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment, Puyao died; in mourning he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Puyao died; Yan's conduct in mourning won praise.

sentences.zh: 起冠軍將軍、司徒左長史、濟陽太守，未拜，遷衞尉，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before he took up the posts he was transferred to be Commandant of the Guard, retaining his generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before accepting those posts he was transferred to Commandant of the Guard, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉太子詹事，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to be steward of the heir apparent's household, with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was made steward of the heir apparent's household with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉丹陽尹，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to be intendant of Danyang, retaining his irregular attendant title.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was made intendant of Danyang, retaining his title as irregular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 晏位任親重，朝夕進見，言論朝事，自豫章王嶷、尚書令王儉皆降意以接之，而晏每以疏漏被上呵責，連稱疾久之。

translations.literal: Yan's position and appointment were intimate and weighty; morning and evening he was received in audience and discussed court affairs. From the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, to the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, all lowered their manner to receive him—but Yan was often rebuked by the emperor for oversights and repeatedly claimed illness for long periods.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held an intimate and weighty position, seeing the emperor morning and evening and discussing state affairs. Even the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, treated him with deference—yet Yan was often rebuked for careless mistakes and repeatedly pleaded illness for extended periods.

sentences.zh: 上以晏須祿養，七年，轉爲江州刺史，晏固辭不願出外，見許，留爲吏部尚書，領太子右衞率。

translations.literal: Because the emperor thought Yan needed salary to support himself, in the seventh year he was transferred to be governor of Jiang Province; Yan firmly declined and did not wish to go outside the capital. Permission was granted, and he was retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor felt Yan needed an income to support himself, so in the seventh year he was appointed governor of Jiang Province. Yan firmly declined to leave the capital; the emperor agreed and kept him on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.

sentences.zh: 終以舊恩見寵。

translations.literal: In the end he was favored because of old kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to enjoy favor on account of their long-standing bond.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王儉雖貴而疏，晏旣領選，權行臺閣，與儉頗不平。

translations.literal: At the time the Director Wang Jian, though eminent, was distant; once Yan headed selection, he exercised power in the secretariat and was rather at odds with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director Wang Jian, though eminent, stood somewhat apart from the emperor; once Yan took charge of personnel selection, he exercised secretariat power and clashed with Jian.

sentences.zh: 儉卒，禮官議諡，上欲依王導諡爲「文獻」，晏啓上曰：「導乃得此諡，但宋以來，不加素族。

translations.literal: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title; the emperor wished to follow Wang Dao and give the title "Literary and Presented," and Yan memorialized the throne, saying: "Dao alone could receive this title, but since the Song, plain families have not been given it."
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title. The emperor wished to follow Wang Dao's example and grant the title "Literary and Presented." Yan memorialized the throne: "Only Dao deserved that title—and since the Song, plain families have not received it."

sentences.zh: 」出謂親人曰：「平頭憲事已行矣。

translations.literal: Going out, he said to his intimates: "The affair of the flat-topped Xian is already done."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the audience, he told his intimates, "That business with flat-top Xian is settled."

sentences.zh: 」八年，改領右衞將軍，陳疾自解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was changed to head the Right Guard, and pleaded illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made to head the Right Guard, then pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 上欲以高宗代晏領選，手敕問之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have Gaozong replace Yan in heading selection, and sent a handwritten edict to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to have Xiao Luan replace Yan in charge of selection and sent a handwritten edict to ask Yan's opinion.

sentences.zh: 晏啓曰：「鸞清幹有餘，然不諳百氏，恐不可居此職。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized: "Luan has more than enough purity and capacity, yet he is not versed in the hundred clans—I fear he cannot hold this office."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Luan is certainly capable and upright, but he is not versed in the great families—I fear he cannot hold this post."

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍中，領太子詹事，本州中正，又以疾辭。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, heading the heir apparent's household and serving as chief assessor of his native province, and again resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made attendant-in-ordinary, head of the heir apparent's household, and chief assessor of his native province, but again resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 十年，改授散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，給親信二十人，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷右僕射，領太孫右衞率。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be right vice director, concurrently heading the heir apparent of the heir apparent's right guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made right vice director, concurrently heading the crown prince's right guard.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，遺旨以尚書事付晏及徐孝嗣，令久於其職。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, his testamentary instruction entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, ordering them to hold their offices long.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wudi died, his testament entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, instructing them to hold their posts for the long term.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，轉左僕射，中正如故。

translations.literal: When Yulin took the throne, Yan was transferred to left vice director, retaining his assessor title.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Yan was made left vice director, retaining his assessor title.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 高宗謀廢立，晏便響應推奉。

translations.literal: When Gaozong plotted deposition and enthronement, Yan at once responded and promoted his elevation.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone himself, Yan immediately supported the move.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，轉尚書令，加後將軍，侍中、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the additional title of rear general; his attendant and assessor titles remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs with the additional title of rear general, retaining his titles as attendant-in-ordinary and chief assessor.

sentences.zh: 封曲江縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang County, with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部，甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: He was given one set of martial music and fifty armed men allowed to enter the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a full set of martial music and fifty armed retainers permitted to enter the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 高宗與晏宴於東府，語及時事，晏扺掌曰：「公常言晏怯，今定何如？

translations.literal: Gaozong feasted with Yan at the Eastern Establishment and spoke of current affairs; Yan clapped his hands and said: "Your Grace always said Yan was timid—how about now?"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in the Eastern Establishment, Gaozong and Yan discussed current affairs. Yan clapped his hands and said, "Your Grace always called me timid—what do you think now?"

sentences.zh: 」建武元年，進號驃騎大將軍，給班劔二十人，侍中、令、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades, and retained his attendant, director, and assessor titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades and retained his titles as attendant-in-ordinary, director, and chief assessor.

sentences.zh: 又加兵百人，領太子少傅，進爵爲公，增邑爲二千戶。

translations.literal: He was further given a hundred troops, made to head the heir apparent's junior mentor, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given a hundred troops, appointed junior mentor of the heir apparent, advanced to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以虜動，給兵千人。

translations.literal: Because the barbarians were active, he was given a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because of northern incursions, he was given an additional thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 晏爲人篤於親舊，爲世祖所稱。

translations.literal: Yan as a man was devoted to kin and old friends, and was praised by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was devoted to kin and old friends, a quality the late emperor had praised.

sentences.zh: 至是自謂佐命惟新，言論常非薄世祖故事，衆始怪之。

translations.literal: From this point he considered himself a founder of the new order; in speech he often disparaged the late emperor's ways, and people first found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he regarded himself as a founder of the new regime and often spoke slightingly of the late emperor's ways, to the astonishment of many.

sentences.zh: 高宗雖以事際須晏，而心相疑斥，料簡世祖中詔，得與晏手敕三百餘紙，皆是論國家事，以此愈猜薄之。

translations.literal: Although Gaozong needed Yan because of the circumstances, in his heart he suspected and rejected him; sorting through the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred sheets of handwritten orders to Yan, all discussing state affairs—by this he grew still more suspicious and cold toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gaozong still needed Yan for the moment, he distrusted him inwardly. Reviewing the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred handwritten orders to Yan on state affairs, which only deepened his suspicion and coldness toward him.

sentences.zh: 初卽位，始安王遙光便勸誅晏，帝曰：「晏於我有勳，且未有罪。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, the Prince of Shian, Yaoguang, at once urged executing Yan; the emperor said: "Yan has merit toward me, and as yet has no crime."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his accession, Prince Yaoguang of Shian urged that Yan be executed. The emperor said, "Yan has served me well, and he has committed no crime."

sentences.zh: 」遙光曰：「晏尚不能爲武帝，安能爲陛下。

translations.literal: Yaoguang said: "If Yan could not even serve Emperor Wu, how can he serve Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang replied, "If he could not even be loyal to Emperor Wu, how can he be loyal to you?"

sentences.zh: 」帝默然變色。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, his expression darkening.

sentences.zh: 時帝常遣心腹左右陳世範等出塗巷採聽異言，由是以晏爲事。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor often sent trusted personal attendants such as Chen Shifan into the lanes to gather and listen for unusual talk; by this they made Yan their target.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sent trusted attendants such as Chen Shifan into the streets to listen for rumors, and through them Yan became the focus of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 晏輕淺無防慮，望開府，數呼相工自視，云當大貴。

translations.literal: Yan was frivolous and without precaution; he hoped for an establishment as a grand minister, repeatedly summoned physiognomists to examine himself, and said he would attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was careless and indiscreet. Hoping for appointment as grand minister, he repeatedly summoned fortune-tellers to read his features and declared that he was destined for great rank.

sentences.zh: 與賔客語，好屏人清間，上聞之，疑晏欲反，遂有誅晏之意。

translations.literal: When speaking with guests he liked to dismiss others for a quiet private talk; when the emperor heard of it, he suspected Yan intended rebellion and thus formed the intention to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When talking with guests he liked to dismiss attendants for private conversation. When the emperor heard of this, he suspected Yan of plotting rebellion and resolved to kill him.

sentences.zh: 傖人鮮于文粲與晏子德元往來，密探朝旨，告晏有異志。

translations.literal: The barbarian-subject Xianyu Wencan had dealings with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored a different will.
translations.idiomatic: The northern subject Xianyu Wencan associated with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 世範等又啓上云：「晏謀因四年南郊，與世祖故舊主帥於道中竊發。

translations.literal: Shifan and others further memorialized the throne: "Yan plots, taking advantage of the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year, to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."
translations.idiomatic: Shifan and others further reported, "Yan plans to use the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."

sentences.zh: 」會虎犯郊壇，帝愈懼。

translations.literal: It happened that a tiger invaded the suburban altar, and the emperor grew still more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When a tiger appeared at the suburban altar, the emperor grew still more alarmed.

sentences.zh: 未郊一日，敕停行。

translations.literal: One day before the sacrifice, an edict halted the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the sacrifice, an edict canceled the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 元會畢，乃召晏於華林省誅之。

translations.literal: When the New Year's audience was finished, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: After the New Year's audience concluded, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「晏閭閻凡伍，少無持操，階緣人乏，班齒官途。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Yan was of common lanes and ordinary ranks, in youth without settled conduct; he climbed by others' want and took his place on the official ladder."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "Yan came from common stock, showed no firm character in youth, and climbed the official ladder by exploiting others' weaknesses."

sentences.zh: 世祖在蕃，搜揚擢用，弃略疵瑕，遂升要重。

translations.literal: When the late emperor was in his princedom, he sought and promoted him, overlooking flaws and blemishes, and thus raised him to crucial weight.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, the late emperor sought him out and promoted him, overlooking his faults, until he rose to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 而輕跳險銳，在貴彌著，猜忌反覆，觸情多端。

translations.literal: Yet he was frivolous, rash, dangerous, and sharp; the higher his rank, the more evident it became—suspicious, changeable, and touching feelings in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was frivolous, rash, and treacherous; the higher he rose, the worse these traits became—suspicious, changeable, and driven by whim.

sentences.zh: 故以兩宮所弗容，十手所共指。

translations.literal: Therefore both palaces could not tolerate him, and ten hands pointed at him together.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason neither palace could tolerate him, and all pointed him out as a danger.

sentences.zh: 旣內愧于心，外懼憲牘，掩迹陳痾，多歷年載。

translations.literal: Having inward shame in his heart and outward fear of the law's documents, he concealed his tracks and claimed illness for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling guilty within and fearing prosecution without, he hid himself behind repeated claims of illness for many years.

sentences.zh: 頻授蕃任，輙辭請不行，事似謙虛，情實詭伏。

translations.literal: Repeatedly given provincial appointments, he always declined and would not go—outwardly seeming modest, inwardly truly deceitful and hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly offered provincial posts, he always declined to leave the capital—an appearance of modesty that masked deceit.

sentences.zh: 隆昌以來，運集艱難，匡贊之功，頗有心力。

translations.literal: Since Longchang, when fortune gathered in hardship, his merit in supporting and assisting showed considerable effort of heart.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Longchang era, when the dynasty faced grave trials, he had contributed real effort to restoring order.

sentences.zh: 迺爵冠通侯，位登元輔，綢繆恩寄，朝莫均焉。

translations.literal: Then his noble rank crowned full marquisates, his office reached chief minister, and intimate favor bound him morning and evening alike.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ennobled as a full marquis, raised to chief minister, and showered with favor morning and evening alike.

sentences.zh: 谿壑可盈，無厭將及。

translations.literal: Ravines and gullies can be filled—his lack of satiety was about to reach its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ravines may be filled, but his greed knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 視天畫地，遂懷異圖。

translations.literal: Looking to heaven and tracing on earth, he then harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: He looked to heaven and plotted on earth, harboring treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 廣求卜相，取信巫覡。

translations.literal: He widely sought divination and physiognomy and put faith in shamans.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out diviners and fortune-tellers and put his faith in shamans.

sentences.zh: 論薦黨附，徧滿臺府。

translations.literal: He discussed recommendations and formed factions until they filled the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He packed the secretariat with his own faction through recommendations and patronage.

sentences.zh: 令大息德元淵藪亡命，同惡相濟，劔客成羣。

translations.literal: He had his eldest son Deyuan harbor fugitives in deep lairs; evildoers aided one another and swordsmen formed gangs.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Deyuan harbored fugitives and outlaws; villains aided one another until swordsmen gathered in gangs.

sentences.zh: 弟詡凶愚，遠相脣齒，信驛往來，密通要契。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was fierce and foolish; from afar they were lip and teeth to each other, with couriers going back and forth and secret communications of crucial pacts.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was brutal and foolish; though far apart, they acted as mutual allies, exchanging couriers and secret agreements.

sentences.zh: 去歲之初，奉朝請鮮于文粲備告姦謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of last year, the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan fully reported the treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: Early last year the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan reported the full details of the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 朕以信必由中，義無與貳，推誠委任，覬能悛改。

translations.literal: We, believing trust must come from within and that in righteousness there is no divided loyalty, extended sincerity and entrusted him, hoping he could reform.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that trust must come from the heart and that loyalty admits no division, We extended Our trust to him, hoping he would reform.

sentences.zh: 而長惡易流，構扇彌大，與北中郎司馬蕭毅、臺隊主劉明達等剋期竊發。

translations.literal: Yet he long cherished evil and easily spread it; his agitation grew ever greater, and with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others he set a date for a surprise rising.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he clung to evil and spread unrest ever wider, setting a date for a surprise rising with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others.

sentences.zh: 以河東王鉉識用微弱，可爲其主，得志之日，當守以虛器。

translations.literal: Taking the Prince of Hedong, Xuan, whose knowledge and capacity were weak, as one who could serve as their lord—on the day they succeeded, he would be kept as an empty vessel.
translations.idiomatic: They intended to make Prince Xuan of Hedong, whose abilities were slight, their puppet ruler, keeping him as a figurehead once they seized power.

sentences.zh: 明達諸辭列，炳然具存。

translations.literal: Mingda's various statements and lists are clear and fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Mingda's confessions and lists of accomplices remain fully on record.

sentences.zh: 昔漢后以反脣致討，魏臣以虯鬚爲戮，況無君之心旣彰，陵上之迹斯著，此而可容，誰寘刑辟。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han empress was punished for turning her lip against authority, and a Wei minister was executed for his curling beard—how much more when a heart without a ruler is already manifest and traces of climbing above one's lord are thus clear: if this can be tolerated, who would be placed within the penal code?
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Han empress was punished for insolent speech and a Wei minister was executed for his arrogance—how much more when disloyalty is plain and the crime of lèse-majesté is evident? If this can be tolerated, who would ever face the law?

sentences.zh: 竝可收付廷尉，肅明國典。」

translations.literal: All may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to clarify the state's statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Let all of them be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that the law may be enforced."

sentences.zh: 晏未敗數日，於北山廟答賽，夜還，晏旣醉，部伍人亦飲酒，羽儀錯亂，前後十餘里中，不復相禁制，識者云「此勢不復久也」。

translations.literal: Several days before Yan's fall, he made a thanksgiving offering at the Beishan temple; returning at night, Yan was already drunk, and his escort men also drank wine—the ceremonial guard fell into disorder, and for more than ten li before and behind, restraint was no longer kept. Observers said, "This power will not last long."
translations.idiomatic: Several days before his downfall, Yan offered thanks at the Beishan temple. Returning at night drunk, with his escort also drinking, his ceremonial guard fell into disorder for more than ten li in every direction. Observers said, "Such power cannot last."

sentences.zh: 晏子德元，有意尚。

translations.literal: Yan's son Deyuan had aspiration and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Deyuan had ability and refinement.

sentences.zh: 至車騎長史。

translations.literal: He reached the post of chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 德元初名湛，世祖謂晏曰：「劉湛、江湛，竝不善終，此非佳名也。

translations.literal: Deyuan's original name was Zhan; the late emperor said to Yan: "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both did not end well—this is not a fine name."
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan's original name was Zhan. The late emperor told Yan, "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both came to bad ends—this is not an auspicious name."

sentences.zh: 」晏乃改之。

translations.literal: Yan then changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then changed his son's name.

sentences.zh: 至是與弟晉安王友德和俱被誅。

translations.literal: At this time he and his younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an's friend Dehe, were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he and his younger brother Dehe, a friend of the Prince of Jin'an, were both executed.

sentences.zh: 晏弟詡，永明中爲少府卿。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Xu, in the Yongming era, was Minister of the Privy Purse.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Xu served as Minister of the Privy Purse during the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 六年，敕位未登黃門郎，不得畜女妓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that those whose rank had not reached Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict declared that officials below the rank of Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 詡與射聲校尉陰玄智坐畜妓免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: Xu and the Archers' Guard colonel Yin Xuanzhi were dismissed from office for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Colonel Yin Xuanzhi of the Archers' Guard were dismissed for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.

sentences.zh: 敕特原詡禁錮。

translations.literal: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.

sentences.zh: 後出爲輔國將軍、始興內史。

translations.literal: Later he went out as General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史劉纘爲奴所殺，詡率郡兵討之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Guang Province, Liu Zuan, was killed by a slave; Xu led commandery troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Administrator Liu Zuan of Guang Province was killed by a slave, Xu led commandery troops to punish the killers.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，授詡持節廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was given the staff of authority as Administrator of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was appointed Administrator of Guang Province with credentials bearing the imperial staff.

sentences.zh: 詡亦篤舊。

translations.literal: Xu, too, was devoted to old ties.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, too, was devoted to old friends and kin.

sentences.zh: 晏誅，上又遣南中郎司馬蕭季敞襲詡殺之。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, the emperor also sent the southern central army's staff officer Xiao Jichang to strike Xu and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's execution, the emperor sent the southern central army's staff officer Xiao Jichang to strike down and kill Xu.

sentences.zh: 蕭諶字彥孚，南蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Chen, courtesy name Yanfu, was a man of Lanling, Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen, courtesy name Yanfu, was a native of Lanling in Southern Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖道清，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoqing was an outside-section gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiao Daoqing served as an outside-section gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父仙伯，桂陽國參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xianbo was a staff officer of the princedom of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Xianbo was a staff officer of the princedom of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 諶初爲州從事，晉熙國侍郎，左常侍。

translations.literal: Chen at first was a provincial aide, a gentleman-attendant of the princedom of Jinxing, and a left regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen began as a provincial aide, then served as gentleman-attendant of the princedom of Jinxing and as left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 諶於太祖爲絕服族子，元徽末，世祖在郢州，欲知京邑消息，太祖遣諶就世祖宣傳謀計，留爲腹心。

translations.literal: Chen to the founding emperor was a clansman beyond the mourning grades; at the end of the Yuanhui era the Heir Apparent was in Ying Province and wished to know news of the capital. The founding emperor sent Chen to the Heir Apparent to convey and transmit plans, and retained him as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a clansman of the founding emperor beyond the mourning grades. At the end of the Yuanhui era, when the future Emperor Wudi was in Ying Province and wished for news from the capital, the founding emperor sent Chen to convey plans and kept him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，爲世祖中軍刑獄參軍，東莞太守。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era he was a penal officer on the Heir Apparent's central army staff and Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era he served as penal officer on the Heir Apparent's central army staff and as Administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 以勳懃封安復縣男，三百戶。

translations.literal: For meritorious service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anfu County, three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anfu with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲武陵王冠軍、臨川王前軍參軍，除尚書都官郎，建威將軍，臨川王鎮西中兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was champion staff officer for the Prince of Wuling and front-army staff officer for the Prince of Linchuan, was appointed Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs for Capital Offenses, made General Who Establishes Might, and central-army officer on the western pacification staff of the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan he served on the staffs of the Princes of Wuling and Linchuan, was appointed Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs for Capital Offenses, made General Who Establishes Might, and central-army officer on the Prince of Linchuan's western pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖在東宮，諶領宿衞。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace, Chen headed night guard.
translations.idiomatic: While the Heir Apparent held court from the Eastern Palace, Chen commanded the night guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖殺張景真，世祖令諶口啓乞景真命，太祖不悅，諶懼而退。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor killed Zhang Jingzhen, the Heir Apparent ordered Chen to plead orally for Jingzhen's life; the founding emperor was displeased, and Chen withdrew in fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor executed Zhang Jingzhen, the Heir Apparent had Chen plead orally for his life. The founding emperor was displeased, and Chen withdrew in fear.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，出諶爲大末令，未之縣，除步兵校尉，領射陽令，轉帶南濮陽太守，領御仗主。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent took the throne, Chen was sent out as magistrate of Damo; before he went to the county he was appointed colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard, concurrently magistrate of Sheyang, then transferred to carry the title of Administrator of southern Puyang, heading the imperial arms guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent ascended the throne, Chen was sent out as magistrate of Damo but never took up the post. He was made colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard and magistrate of Sheyang, then transferred to Administrator of southern Puyang while heading the imperial arms guard.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，爲南蘭陵太守，建威將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was Administrator of Southern Lanling, retaining his title as General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was made Administrator of Southern Lanling, retaining his rank as General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 復除步兵校尉，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard, retaining his administrator title.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard while retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 世祖齋內兵仗悉付之，心膂密事，皆使參掌。

translations.literal: The late emperor entrusted to him all arms within the fasting palace, and had him take part in confidential matters of heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor entrusted him with all arms within the fasting palace and had him participate in the most confidential affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 除正員郎，轉左中郎將，後軍將軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed a full-rank gentleman, transferred to be left central army general, rear army general, and retained his administrator title.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a full-rank gentleman, then made left central army general and rear army general while retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 世祖卧疾延昌殿，敕諶在左右宿直。

translations.literal: When the late emperor lay ill in the Yan-chang Hall, he ordered Chen to keep night watch at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor fell ill in the Yanchang Hall, he ordered Chen to keep night watch at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 上崩，遺敕諶領殿內事如舊。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, his testament ordered Chen to head palace-hall affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's death, his testament ordered Chen to continue managing palace affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，深委信諶，諶每請急出宿，帝通夕不得寐，諶還乃安。

translations.literal: When Yulin took the throne, he deeply entrusted and trusted Chen; whenever Chen asked urgently to go out for night duty, the emperor could not sleep all night until Chen returned, and only then was he at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, he placed deep trust in Chen. Whenever Chen asked to go out on night duty, the emperor could not sleep until Chen returned.

sentences.zh: 轉衞軍司馬，兼衞尉，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be marshal of the Guard Army, concurrently Commandant of the Guard, with the additional title of General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was made marshal of the Guard Army and Commandant of the Guard, with the additional title of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，敕還復本任，守衞尉。

translations.literal: When his mother died, an edict recalled him to resume his former duties, retaining the Commandant of the Guard post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict recalled him from mourning to resume his former duties as Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，有所匡諫，帝旣在後宮不出，唯遣諶及蕭坦之遙進，乃得聞達。

translations.literal: When Gaozong assisted in government and offered correction and remonstrance, the emperor stayed in the rear palace and did not come out; only by sending Chen and Xiao Tanzhi to advance from afar could his words be heard and conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan served as regent and offered remonstrance, the young emperor stayed in the rear palace and would not emerge; only by sending Chen and Xiao Tanzhi to relay his words could he be reached.

sentences.zh: 諶回附高宗，勸行廢立，密召諸王典籤約語之，不許諸王外接人物。

translations.literal: Chen turned to attach himself to Gaozong, urged carrying out deposition and enthronement, secretly summoned the princes' recorders to bind them by agreement, and did not permit the princes to receive people from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Chen aligned himself with Xiao Luan, urged the deposition and enthronement, secretly summoned the princes' recorders to bind them by pact, and forbade the princes from receiving outsiders.

sentences.zh: 諶親要日久，衆皆憚而從之。

translations.literal: Chen had been intimate and important for many days; all feared him and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had long been intimate with power, and all feared him and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 鬱林被廢日，初聞外有變，猶密爲手敕呼諶，其見信如此。

translations.literal: On the day Yulin was deposed, when he first heard there was trouble outside, he still secretly wrote a handwritten edict summoning Chen—such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Emperor Yulin was deposed, when he first heard of trouble outside, he still secretly wrote a handwritten edict summoning Chen—such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 諶性險進無計略，及廢帝日，領兵先入後宮，齋內仗身素隷服諶，莫有動者。

translations.literal: Chen's nature was dangerous and aggressive without strategy; on the day the emperor was deposed, he led troops first into the rear palace. The armed attendants within the fasting palace had long been subordinate to Chen, and none stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was treacherous and rash but lacked strategic sense. On the day of the deposition he led troops first into the rear palace; the armed attendants of the fasting palace had long been his men, and none resisted.

sentences.zh: 海陵立，轉中領軍，進爵爲公，二千戶。

translations.literal: When Hailing was enthroned, Chen was transferred to central palace guard general, advanced in rank to duke, two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing was enthroned, Chen was made central palace guard general, advanced to duke, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 甲仗五十人。

translations.literal: Fifty armed men.
translations.idiomatic: He was given fifty armed retainers.

sentences.zh: 入直殿內，月十日還府。

translations.literal: He entered duty within the palace halls; every month on the tenth day he returned to his establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He kept watch within the palace halls, returning to his residence on the tenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，轉領軍將軍，左將軍，南徐州刺史，給扶，進爵衡陽郡公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was transferred to palace guard general, left general, governor of southern Xu Province, given a staff for support, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he was made palace guard general and left general, appointed governor of southern Xu Province with a support staff, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高宗初許事克用諶爲揚州，及有此授，諶恚曰：「見炊飯熟，推以與人。

translations.literal: Gaozong had at first promised that when the affair succeeded Chen would be used for Yang Province; when this appointment came instead, Chen said in anger: "Seeing the cooked rice ready, you push the pot to someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan had initially promised Chen the governorship of Yang Province once the coup succeeded; when this lesser appointment came instead, Chen said angrily, "You see the rice cooked and hand the pot to someone else."

sentences.zh: 」王晏聞之曰：「誰復爲蕭諶作甌箸者。

translations.literal: Wang Yan heard of it and said: "Who will make bowls and chopsticks for Xiao Chen again?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan heard of it and said, "Who will set the table for Xiao Chen now?"

sentences.zh: 」諶恃勳重，干豫朝政，諸有選用，輙命議尚書使爲申論。

translations.literal: Chen relied on the weight of his merit and interfered in court government; whenever there were selections and appointments, he always ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to argue the case for him.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his meritorious service, Chen meddled in court affairs; whenever there were appointments, he ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 上新卽位，遣左右要人於外聽察，具知諶言，深相疑阻。

translations.literal: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted personal attendants outside to listen and observe, fully learned Chen's words, and deeply suspected and blocked him.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted attendants to listen in the capital, learned all of Chen's remarks, and grew deeply suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，上幸華林園，宴諶及尚書令王晏等數人盡歡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, the Director Wang Yan, and several others to full merriment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, Director Wang Yan, and several others until all were merry.

sentences.zh: 坐罷，留諶晚出，至華林閤，仗身執還入省，上遣左右莫智明數諶曰：「隆昌之際，非卿無有今日。

translations.literal: When the seating ended, he kept Chen to leave late; reaching the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to enumerate to Chen: "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today."
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, the emperor kept Chen behind. At the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to tell Chen, "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today for me."

sentences.zh: 今一門二州，兄弟三封，朝廷相報，政可極此。

translations.literal: Now one household holds two provinces, three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can rightly reach only this far.
translations.idiomatic: Now your household holds two provinces and three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can go no further than this.

sentences.zh: 卿恒懷怨望，乃云炊飯已熟，合甑與人邪？

translations.literal: You constantly harbor resentment, and even say the cooked rice is ready—should the pot be given to others?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you constantly harbor resentment, even saying the rice is cooked and asking whether the pot should be handed to others?

sentences.zh: 今賜卿死。

translations.literal: Now We grant you death.
translations.idiomatic: Now We grant you death.

sentences.zh: 」諶謂智明曰：「天去人亦復不遠，我與至尊殺高、武諸王，是君傳語來去。

translations.literal: Chen said to Zhiming: "Heaven and man are not far apart; I and the Supreme One killed the princes of Gao and Wu—it was you who passed messages back and forth."
translations.idiomatic: Chen told Zhiming, "Heaven is not far from man. I and the emperor killed the princes of Gao and Wu—you were the one who carried messages between us."

sentences.zh: 我今死，還取卿。

translations.literal: I die today—you will be taken next.
translations.idiomatic: I die today—you will be next.

sentences.zh: 」於省殺之，至秋而智明死，見諶爲祟。

translations.literal: He was killed in the secretariat; by autumn Zhiming died, seeing Chen as a haunting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed in the secretariat. By autumn Zhiming died, claiming that Chen's ghost was haunting him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蕭諶擢自凡庸，識用輕險，因藉倖會，早預驅馳。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Xiao Chen was raised from the commonplace, his knowledge and conduct frivolous and dangerous; relying on fortunate chance, he early joined the driven ranks."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Xiao Chen rose from common stock, his talents frivolous and dangerous; by fortunate chance he early joined the emperor's service."

sentences.zh: 永明之季，曲頒恩紀。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming, favor was bent and bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming he was showered with special favor.

sentences.zh: 鬱林昏悖，頗立誠效。

translations.literal: Yulin was benighted and perverse, yet Chen showed considerable loyal effect.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Yulin was benighted and perverse, Chen rendered loyal service.

sentences.zh: 寵靈優渥，期遇兼隆，內總戎柄，外暢蕃威，兄弟榮貴，震灼朝野。

translations.literal: Favor and blessing were rich and deep, his appointed meetings doubly exalted; within he held the military handle, without he extended princely power; his brothers were honored and eminent, dazzling court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He was showered with favor, held military power within and provincial authority without; his brothers were ennobled, and their glory dazzled court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 曾不感佩殊荷，少答萬一。

translations.literal: He never felt moved by special grace or repaid even one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never felt gratitude and repaid scarcely a fraction of what he owed.

sentences.zh: 自以勳高伊、霍，事均難賞，才冠當時，恥居物後。

translations.literal: He considered his merit higher than Yi Yin and Huo Guang, his deeds equal to what is hard to reward, his talent foremost in the age, and was ashamed to stand behind others.
translations.idiomatic: He deemed his merit greater than Yi Yin and Huo Guang's, his deeds beyond reward, his talent unmatched in the age—and was ashamed to stand behind others.

sentences.zh: 矯制王權，與奪由己。

translations.literal: He falsified the royal system and made giving and taking depend on himself.
translations.idiomatic: He usurped royal authority, making appointments at his own will.

sentences.zh: 空懷疑懼，坐構嫌猜。

translations.literal: Emptily harboring suspicion and fear, he sat and built up dislike and mistrust.
translations.idiomatic: Harborng groundless suspicion and fear, he bred distrust.

sentences.zh: 覘候宮掖，希覬非望。

translations.literal: He spied on the palace women's quarters and hoped for what was not his due.
translations.idiomatic: He spied on the inner palace and coveted what was not his due.

sentences.zh: 蔽上罔下之心，誣君不臣之迹，固以彰暴民聽，喧聒遐邇。

translations.literal: A heart that screened the ruler and deceived those below, traces of slandering the lord and disloyalty to subjecthood—these were already manifest to the violent populace's hearing and clamorous near and far.
translations.idiomatic: His heart screened the ruler and deceived those below; his disloyalty was plain to all, and rumor of it spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 遂潛散金帛，招集不逞，交結禁衞，互爲脣齒，密契戚邸，將肆姦逆。

translations.literal: Then he secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered the unbridled, joined with the palace guard, became lip and teeth to one another, made secret pacts with imperial kin establishments, and was about to unleash treachery and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered malcontents, won over the palace guard, made secret pacts with imperial kin, and was about to launch treason.

sentences.zh: 朕以其任寄旣重，爵列河山，每加彌縫，弘以大信，庶能懷音，翻然悛改。

translations.literal: We, because his commission was already weighty and his noble rank listed among the hills and rivers, repeatedly added smoothing patches and extended great trust, hoping he could embrace good faith and suddenly reform.
translations.idiomatic: Because his commission was weighty and his rank eminent, We repeatedly smoothed matters over and extended great trust, hoping he would reform.

sentences.zh: 而豺狼其性，凶謀滋甚。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was that of wolf and jackal, and his vicious plots grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his wolfish nature only grew worse, and his treacherous plots intensified.

sentences.zh: 夫無將必戮，陽秋明義，況釁積禍盈，若斯之大。

translations.literal: When there is no general, execution is certain—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when offenses accumulated and calamity overflowed to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion is afoot, execution is inevitable—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when guilt had accumulated to such a degree.

sentences.zh: 可收付廷尉，速正刑書。

translations.literal: He may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to swiftly rectify the penal documents.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that sentence may be swiftly pronounced.

sentences.zh: 罪止元惡，餘無所問。」

translations.literal: Guilt stops at the chief villain; the rest are not to be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Punishment shall fall only on the chief villain; the rest shall not be questioned."

sentences.zh: 諶好左道，吳興沈文猷相諶云：「相不減高帝。

translations.literal: Chen loved heterodox ways; Shen Wenyao of Wuxing physiognomized Chen and said: "Your physiognomy is not less than the High Emperor's."
translations.idiomatic: Chen dabbled in heterodox arts. Shen Wenyao of Wuxing read his features and said, "Your physiognomy is no less than the founding emperor's."

sentences.zh: 」諶喜曰：「感卿意，無爲人言也。

translations.literal: Chen was pleased and said: "I am moved by your intent—do not speak of this to others."
translations.idiomatic: Chen was pleased and said, "I am moved by your words—tell no one."

sentences.zh: 」至是文猷伏誅。

translations.literal: At this time Wenyao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wenyao was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 諶兄誕，字彥偉，初爲殿中將軍。

translations.literal: Chen's elder brother Dan, courtesy name Yanwei, at first was a palace hall general.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's elder brother Xiao Dan, courtesy name Yanwei, began as a palace hall general.

sentences.zh: 永明中爲建康令，與秣陵令司馬迪之同乘行，車前導四卒，左丞沈昭略奏：「凡有鹵簿官，共乘不得兼列騶寺。

translations.literal: In Yongming he was magistrate of Jiankang; riding together with the Moling magistrate Sima Dizhi, with four soldiers leading before the carriage, the left assistant director Shen Zhaolue memorialized: "Whenever officials with ceremonial guards share a carriage, they may not jointly array outriders and attendants."
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming he was magistrate of Jiankang. Riding with the Moling magistrate Sima Dizhi, each with four soldiers leading his carriage, the left assistant director Shen Zhaolue memorialized, "Officials with ceremonial guards may not jointly array outriders when riding together."

sentences.zh: 請免誕等官。

translations.literal: He requested dismissal of Dan and others from office.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that Dan and the others be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 」詔贖論。

translations.literal: An edict ordered redemption and debate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed them to commute the penalty by fine.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，自輔國徐州爲持節督司州剌史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, from General Who Assists the State in Xu Province he was made governor of Si Province bearing the staff of authority, retaining his general title.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was transferred from General Who Assists the State in Xu Province to Governor of Si Province with credentials bearing the imperial staff, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，封安德侯，五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ande, five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ande with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進號冠軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Champion.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to Champion General.

sentences.zh: 建武二年春，虜攻司州，誕盡力拒守，虜退。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, the barbarians attacked Si Province; Dan exhausted his strength in defense, and the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, the northern enemy attacked Si Province. Dan defended with all his strength until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 增封四百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 徵左衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 上欲殺諶，以誕在邊鎮拒虜，故未及行。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to kill Chen, but because Dan was on the frontier garrison resisting the barbarians, the deed was not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to kill Chen, but because Dan was on the frontier resisting the enemy, he delayed.

sentences.zh: 虜退六旬，諶誅，遣黃門郎梁王爲司州別駕，使誅誕，束身受戮，家口繫尚方。

translations.literal: Sixty days after the barbarians withdrew, Chen was executed; the Yellow Gate Gentleman Liang Wang was sent as Si Province assistant administrator to execute Dan. He bound himself and accepted execution; his household was detained at the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty days after the enemy withdrew, Chen was executed. The emperor sent the Yellow Gate Gentleman Liang Wang as assistant administrator of Si Province to execute Dan. Dan submitted to execution, and his household was detained at the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 諶弟誄，與諶同豫廢立，爲寧朔將軍、東莞太守，轉西中郎司馬。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Tui, who with Chen alike took part in deposition and enthronement, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dongguan, then transferred to be staff officer of the western central army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Xiao Tui, who had taken part with Chen in the deposition and enthronement, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dongguan, then transferred to staff officer of the western central army.

sentences.zh: 建武初，封西昌侯，千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang, a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉太子左率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be the heir apparent's left guard leader.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left guard leader of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 領軍解司州圍還，同伏誅。

translations.literal: When the palace guard general lifted the siege of Si Province and returned, he was executed together with the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace guard general lifted the siege of Si Province and returned, Tui was executed along with the others.

sentences.zh: 諶伯父仙民，官至太中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Chen's father's elder brother Xianmin reached the post of Grand Master of the Palace, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's uncle Xiao Xianmin rose to Grand Master of the Palace and died in office.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之，南蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi was a man of Lanling, Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi was a native of Lanling in Southern Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖道濟，太中大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoji was Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiao Daoji served as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 父欣祖，有勳於世祖，至武進令。

translations.literal: His father Xinzu had merit toward the late emperor and reached the post of magistrate of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Xinzu had rendered meritorious service to the late emperor and rose to magistrate of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 坦之與蕭諶同族。

translations.literal: Tanzhi and Xiao Chen were of the same clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was of the same clan as Xiao Chen.

sentences.zh: 初爲殿中將軍，累至世祖中軍板刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a palace hall general, and by stages reached penal officer on the board of the late emperor's central army staff.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a palace hall general and eventually became penal officer on the board of the late emperor's central army staff.

sentences.zh: 以宗族見驅使。

translations.literal: Because of clan ties he was seen and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He was employed on account of his clan connection.

sentences.zh: 除竟陵王鎮北征北參軍，東宮直閤，以懃直爲世祖所知。

translations.literal: He was appointed northern expedition staff officer on the northern pacification staff of the Prince of Jingling and a direct attendant of the Eastern Palace; for diligent duty he was known to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed staff officer on the northern expedition staff of the Prince of Jingling and direct attendant of the Eastern Palace; his diligent service won the late emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 除給事中，淮陵令，又除蘭陵令，給事中如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervisor of attendance, magistrate of Huailing, then again magistrate of Lanling, retaining his supervisor title.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervisor of attendance and magistrate of Huailing, then magistrate of Lanling while retaining his title as supervisor of attendance.

sentences.zh: 尚書起部郎，司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs for Establishment, and central-army staff officer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs for Establishment and central-army staff officer of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，坦之隨太孫文武度上臺，除射聲校尉，令如故。

translations.literal: When the late emperor died, Tanzhi followed the heir apparent of the heir apparent's civil and military officers in crossing to the upper terrace; he was appointed colonel of the Archers' Guard, retaining his magistrate title.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor died, Tanzhi accompanied the crown prince's officials to the upper terrace. He was appointed colonel of the Archers' Guard while retaining his post as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 未拜，除正員郎、南魯郡太守。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment, he was appointed full-rank gentleman and Administrator of Nanlu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was appointed full-rank gentleman and Administrator of Nanlu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗謀廢少帝，旣與蕭諶及坦之定謀。

translations.literal: When Gaozong plotted to depose the young emperor, he had already fixed the plan with Xiao Chen and Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan plotted to depose the young emperor, he had already settled the plan with Xiao Chen and Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝腹心直閤將軍曹道剛疑外間有異，密有處分，諶未能發。

translations.literal: The emperor's trusted direct-attendant general Cao Daogang suspected something unusual outside and secretly made dispositions; Chen could not launch the action.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's trusted direct-attendant general Cao Daogang suspected trouble outside and secretly took precautions; Chen could not act.

sentences.zh: 始興內史蕭季敞、南陽太守蕭穎基竝應還都，諶欲待二蕭至，藉其勢力以舉事。

translations.literal: The interior minister of Shixing, Xiao Jichang, and the Administrator of Nanyang, Xiao Yingji, were both due to return to the capital; Chen wished to wait until the two Xiaos arrived and borrow their power to raise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The interior minister of Shixing, Xiao Jichang, and the Administrator of Nanyang, Xiao Yingji, were both due to return to the capital. Chen wished to wait for them and rely on their forces to act.

sentences.zh: 高宗慮事變，以告坦之，坦之馳謂諶曰：「廢天子古來大事。

translations.literal: Gaozong feared the affair would change; he told Tanzhi, and Tanzhi galloped to tell Chen: "Deposing the Son of Heaven is from ancient times a great matter."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan feared the plot might unravel and told Tanzhi. Tanzhi galloped to Chen and said, "Deposing the Son of Heaven is a grave matter in any age."

sentences.zh: 比聞曹道剛、朱隆之等轉已猜疑。

translations.literal: Recently I hear Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi, and others are growing suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi, and others are growing suspicious.

sentences.zh: 衞尉明日若不就事，無所復及。

translations.literal: If the Commandant of the Guard does not act tomorrow, nothing more can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If you as Commandant of the Guard do not act tomorrow, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 弟有百歲母，豈能坐聽禍敗，政應作餘計耳！

translations.literal: Your younger brother has a mother of a hundred years—how can he sit and listen to disaster and ruin? He ought to make other plans!
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother has a mother nearing a hundred—can he sit by while disaster strikes? You must act at once!

sentences.zh: 」諶遑遽，明日遂廢帝，坦之力也。

translations.literal: Chen was flustered and hurried; the next day he deposed the emperor—it was Tanzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was thrown into confusion; the next day he deposed the emperor—thanks to Tanzhi's urging.

sentences.zh: 海陵卽位，除黃門郎、兼衞尉卿、進爵伯，增邑爲六百戶。

translations.literal: When Hailing took the throne, Tanzhi was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, concurrently Commandant of the Guard, advanced to baron, and his fief increased to six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing took the throne, Tanzhi was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman and Commandant of the Guard, advanced to baron, with his fief increased to six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，遷散騎常侍，右衞將軍，進爵侯，增邑爲千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was transferred to irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General of the Right Guard, advanced to marquis, and his fief increased to fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he was made irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General of the Right Guard, advanced to marquis, with his fief increased to fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年，虜動，假坦之節，督徐州征討軍事。

translations.literal: The next year, when the barbarians were active, Tanzhi was given credentials and put in charge of Xu Province's campaign and punitive military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the northern enemy attacked, Tanzhi was given credentials and placed in command of Xu Province's campaign forces.

sentences.zh: 虜圍鍾離，春斷淮洲，坦之擊破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians besieged Zhongli and in spring cut off the Huai islets; Tanzhi struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy besieged Zhongli and in spring severed the Huai River islets; Tanzhi defeated them.

sentences.zh: 還加領太子中庶子，未拜，遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On returning he was additionally appointed to concurrently serve as Grand Master of the Central Palace Personnel for the Crown Prince; before he took up the appointment, he was transferred to General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Central Palace Personnel for the Crown Prince, but before he could take up the post he was transferred to General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，爲侍中、領軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 東昏立，爲侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Donghun was enthroned, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun was enthroned, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，遭母喪，起復職，加右將軍，置府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he suffered his mother's death; recalled from mourning to resume office, he was given the additional title General of the Right and an official headquarters was established for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan, when his mother died, he was recalled from mourning to resume office, given the additional title of General of the Right, and granted an official staff.

sentences.zh: 江祏兄弟欲立始安王遙光，密謂坦之，坦之曰：「明帝取天下，已非次第，天下人至今不服。

translations.literal: The brothers Jiang Shi wished to enthrone Prince Yaoguang of Shian and secretly told Tanzhi; Tanzhi said: "When Ming Di seized the empire, it was already out of proper succession, and people under heaven to this day do not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Shi brothers wanted to enthrone Prince Yaoguang of Shian and secretly told Tanzhi. Tanzhi said, "When Emperor Ming seized the throne, it was already a violation of proper succession, and the people have never accepted it.

sentences.zh: 今若復作此事，恐四海瓦解。

translations.literal: If we do this again now, I fear the four seas will disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: If we attempt this again, I fear the realm will fall apart.

sentences.zh: 我其不敢言。

translations.literal: I certainly dare not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not have any part in it.

sentences.zh: 」持喪還宅。

translations.literal: He maintained his mourning and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 宅在東府城東，遙光起事，遣人夜掩取坦之，坦之科頭著褌踰牆走，從東冶僦渡南渡，間道還臺，假節督衆軍討遙光，屯湘宮寺。

translations.literal: His residence was east of the Eastern Palace quarter. When Yaoguang raised the affair, he sent men by night to seize Tanzhi secretly. Tanzhi, with bare head and wearing only drawers, climbed over the wall and fled. He took a rented boat from the Eastern Smeltery to cross the Nan Du ferry, returned to the capital by a back road, was given credentials to supervise all the armies in punishing Yaoguang, and encamped at Xiangong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His house lay east of the Eastern Palace quarter. When Yaoguang launched his revolt, he sent men by night to seize Tanzhi. Tanzhi fled bareheaded in his underdrawers, climbing over a wall. He hired a boat at the Eastern Smeltery to cross the Nan Du ferry, returned to the capital by a hidden route, was granted credentials to command the armies against Yaoguang, and encamped at Xiangong Temple.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷尚書右僕射，丹陽尹，右將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Intendant of Danyang, retaining his post as General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was suppressed, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Intendant of Danyang, retaining his rank as General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 進爵公，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to duke and his fief increased by a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as duke and his fief was increased by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 坦之肥黑無鬚，語聲嘶，時人號爲「蕭瘂」。

translations.literal: Tanzhi was fat and dark, without a beard; his speech was hoarse, and people of the time called him "Xiao the Hoarse."
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was stout and dark-skinned, beardless; his voice was hoarse, and people called him "Xiao the Hoarse."

sentences.zh: 剛佷專執，羣小畏而憎之。

translations.literal: He was fierce, stubborn, and autocratic; the petty men feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, stubborn, and domineering, he was feared and loathed by court sycophants.

sentences.zh: 遙光事平二十餘日，帝遣延明主帥黃文濟領兵圍坦之宅，殺之。

translations.literal: More than twenty days after Yaoguang's affair was settled, the emperor sent the Yanming camp commander Huang Wenji at the head of troops to surround Tanzhi's residence and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: A little over twenty days after Yaoguang's revolt was suppressed, the emperor sent the Yanming camp commander Huang Wenji with troops to surround Tanzhi's house and kill him.

sentences.zh: 子賞，祕書郎。

translations.literal: His son Shang was a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shang served as secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亦伏誅。

translations.literal: He too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was also executed.

sentences.zh: 坦之從兄翼宗，爲海陵郡，將發。

translations.literal: Tanzhi's older cousin of his clan branch Yizong was magistrate of Hailing Commandery and was about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi's cousin Yizong served as magistrate of Hailing Commandery and was about to set out.

sentences.zh: 坦之謂文濟曰：「從兄海陵宅故應無他？

translations.literal: Tanzhi said to Wenji: "My cousin the Hailing magistrate's household should surely be without other trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi said to Wenji, "My cousin the magistrate of Hailing—his household ought to be free of involvement, yes?

sentences.zh: 」文濟曰：「海陵宅在何處？

translations.literal: Wenji said: "Where is the Hailing magistrate's residence?
translations.idiomatic: Wenji asked, "Where is the Hailing magistrate's residence?

sentences.zh: 」坦之告。

translations.literal: Tanzhi told him.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi told him.

sentences.zh: 文濟曰：「應得罪。

translations.literal: Wenji said: "He ought to be guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Wenji said, "Then he must be guilty."

sentences.zh: 」仍遣收之。

translations.literal: He then sent men to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent men to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 檢家赤貧，唯有質錢帖子數百，還以啓帝，原死，繫尚方。

translations.literal: Searching the household, they found extreme poverty—only several hundred pawn-ticket notes—and reported this to the emperor, who spared him from death and imprisoned him in the Directorate of Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: A search found the family utterly destitute, with only a few hundred pawn tickets; the report reached the emperor, who spared Yizong's life and confined him to the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 和帝中興元年，追贈坦之中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Emperor He, Tanzhi was posthumously enfeoffed as General of the Central Army with credentials equal to those of the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing under Emperor He, Tanzhi was posthumously honored as General of the Central Army with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 江祏字弘業，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi, courtesy name Hongye, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi, courtesy name Hongye, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖遵，寧朔參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zun was a staff officer of Ningshuo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiang Zun served as Ningshuo staff officer.

sentences.zh: 父德隣，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His father Delin was Right Senior Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Delin served as Right Senior Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 祏姑爲景皇后，少爲高宗所親，恩如兄弟。

translations.literal: Shi's paternal aunt was Empress Jing; from youth he was close to Gaozong, their favor being like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's aunt was Empress Jing; from youth he was intimate with Xiao Luan, and they treated each other with the affection of brothers.

sentences.zh: 宋末，解褐晉熙國常侍，太祖徐州西曹，員外郎，高宗冠軍參軍，帶灄陽令，竟陵王征北參軍，尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, he entered service as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Jinxi, then Western Assistant of Xu Province under the Taizu, then Vice Gentleman, then a staff officer of the Champion General under Gaozong while concurrently serving as Magistrate of Ziyang, then a northern-campaign staff officer under the King of Jingling, and Gentleman of the Water Section in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Liu Song dynasty, he began his career as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Jinxi, then served as Western Assistant of Xu Province under Emperor Gao, Vice Gentleman, staff officer to the Champion General under Xiao Luan while also serving as Magistrate of Ziyang, northern-campaign staff officer under the King of Jingling, and Gentleman of the Water Section in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高宗爲吳興，以祏爲郡丞，加宣威將軍，廬陵王中軍功曹記室，安陸王左軍諮議，領錄事，帶京兆太守。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was at Wuxing, he made Shi the deputy magistrate of the commandery, with the additional title General Who Spreads Majesty, recorder-clerk in the central-army staff office of the King of Luling, left-army adviser to the King of Anlu while concurrently recorder of affairs and Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan served at Wuxing, he appointed Shi deputy magistrate of the commandery with the additional title General Who Spreads Majesty, recorder-clerk in the central-army staff office of the King of Luling, and left-army adviser to the King of Anlu while also serving as recorder of affairs and Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 除通直郎，補南徐州別駕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of Direct Communication and assigned as Vice Administrator of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of Direct Communication and assigned as Vice Administrator of Southern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，遷右衞將軍，掌甲仗廉察。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, in charge of armor and weapons and their inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was made General of the Right Guard, responsible for the oversight and inspection of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 祏以外戚親要，勢冠當時，遠致餉遺，或取諸王第名書好物。
