translations.literal: Shi, as a close and important maternal kinsman, stood above all of his time in power; gifts were sent to him from afar, or he took fine goods registered by name from the princes' mansions.
translations.idiomatic: As a powerful maternal kinsman of the imperial house, Shi stood at the apex of his age; gifts poured in from afar, and he sometimes took prized goods registered by name from the princes' residences.

sentences.zh: 然家行甚睦，待子姪有恩意。

translations.literal: Yet in family conduct he was very harmonious and treated sons and nephews with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within his household he was deeply harmonious and treated his sons and nephews with genuine affection.

sentences.zh: 上寢疾，永泰元年，轉祏爲侍中、中書令，出入殿省。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell gravely ill, in the first year of Yongtai Shi was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat, entering and leaving the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, in the first year of Yongtai Shi was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat, with free access to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上崩，遺詔轉右僕射，祏弟衞尉祀爲侍中，敬皇后弟劉暄爲衞尉。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the deathbed edict transferred him to Right Vice Director; Shi's younger brother Si, Commandant of the Guard, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Empress Jing's younger brother Liu Xuan was made Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the deathbed edict made Shi Right Vice Director; Shi's younger brother Si, Commandant of the Guard, was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Empress Jing's younger brother Liu Xuan was made Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，參掌選事。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne, he shared in managing selections and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun took the throne, Shi shared in managing official appointments.

sentences.zh: 高宗雖顧命羣公，而意寄多在祏兄弟。

translations.literal: Although Gaozong entrusted the group of lords on his deathbed, his true reliance was mostly on the Shi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiao Luan entrusted several senior officials on his deathbed, his real confidence rested chiefly on the Shi brothers.

sentences.zh: 至是更直殿內，動止關諮。

translations.literal: From then on they took turns staying on duty inside the palace halls; the emperor's every move required their consultation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they took turns on duty inside the palace, and the emperor's every move required their approval.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he concurrently served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he additionally served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 劉暄遷散騎常侍，右衞將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan was transferred to irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was made irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 祏兄弟與暄及始安王遙光、尚書令徐孝嗣、領軍蕭坦之六人，更日帖敕，時呼爲「六貴」。

translations.literal: Shi and his brother, together with Xuan, Prince Yaoguang of Shian, Director of the Department of State Affairs Xu Xiaosi, and General of the Guard Xiao Tanzhi—six men in all—took turns daily issuing edicts, and people of the time called them the "Six Exalted Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Shi and his brother, together with Liu Xuan, Prince Yaoguang of Shian, Director of the Department of State Affairs Xu Xiaosi, and General of the Guard Xiao Tanzhi—the six of them took turns issuing edicts each day, and people called them the "Six Exalted Ones."

sentences.zh: 帝稍欲行意，孝嗣不能奪，坦之雖時有異同，而祏堅意執制，帝深忿之。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually wished to act on his own inclinations; Xiaosi could not overrule him; although Tanzhi sometimes differed, Shi firmly restrained him, and the emperor deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually wished to have his own way. Xu Xiaosi could not overrule him; Tanzhi sometimes disagreed, but Shi firmly held him in check, and the emperor deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 帝失德旣彰，祏議欲立江夏王寶玄。

translations.literal: The emperor's misconduct already being manifest, Shi proposed enthrone Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's misconduct became unmistakable, Shi proposed enthrone Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 劉暄初爲寶玄郢州行事，執事過刻。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan had initially served as acting administrator of Ying Province for Bao Xuan and was excessively harsh in conducting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan had initially served as acting administrator of Ying Province for Bao Xuan and was excessively severe in his conduct of affairs.

sentences.zh: 有人獻馬，寶玄欲看之，暄曰：「馬何用看。

translations.literal: Someone presented a horse; Bao Xuan wished to look at it, and Xuan said: "What use is there in looking at a horse?
translations.idiomatic: When someone presented a horse, Bao Xuan wished to see it, but Xuan said, "What is the point of looking at a horse?

sentences.zh: 」妃索煮肫，帳下諮暄，暄曰：「旦已煮鵝，不煩復此。

translations.literal: The princess consort asked for gizzards to be boiled; the staff consulted Xuan, and Xuan said: "This morning goose has already been boiled—no need for this again.
translations.idiomatic: The princess consort asked for gizzards to be cooked; the household staff consulted Xuan, who said, "Goose was already cooked this morning—there is no need for this as well.

sentences.zh: 」寶玄恚曰：「舅殊無渭陽之情。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan said in anger: "My uncle shows absolutely no affection of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan said angrily, "My uncle shows not the slightest affection of kinship."

sentences.zh: 」暄聞之亦不悅。

translations.literal: When Xuan heard this he too was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan heard this, he too was displeased.

sentences.zh: 至是不同祏議，欲立建安王寶夤，密謀於遙光。

translations.literal: At this point he opposed Shi's plan and wished to enthrone Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an, plotting secretly with Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he opposed Shi's plan and wished to enthrone Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an, conspiring secretly with Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 遙光自以年長，屬當鼎命，微旨動祏。

translations.literal: Yaoguang, considering himself the elder and that the mandate should fall to him, hinted his intentions to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang, considering himself the senior candidate and the rightful heir to the throne, subtly pressed Shi.

sentences.zh: 祏弟祀以少主難保，勸祏立遙光。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Si, believing the young ruler could not be preserved, urged Shi to enthrone Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Si, believing the young emperor could not be preserved, urged Shi to enthrone Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 暄以遙光若立，己失元舅之望，不肯同。

translations.literal: Xuan feared that if Yaoguang were enthroned he would lose his hope as primary maternal uncle, and refused to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan feared that if Yaoguang were enthroned he would lose his standing as chief maternal uncle, and refused to agree.

sentences.zh: 故祏遲疑久不決。

translations.literal: Thus Shi hesitated for a long time and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shi hesitated for a long time and could reach no decision.

sentences.zh: 遙光大怒，遣左右黃曇慶於清溪橋道中刺殺暄，曇慶見暄部伍人多，不敢發。

translations.literal: Yaoguang was greatly angered and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing to assassinate Xuan on the road at Qingxi Bridge; Tanqing saw Xuan's retinue was numerous and dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang was furious and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing to assassinate Xuan on the road at Qingxi Bridge, but Tanqing saw that Xuan's escort was too large and dared not act.

sentences.zh: 事覺，暄告祏謀，帝處分收祏兄弟。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Xuan reported Shi's plot; the emperor ordered the arrest of the Shi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Xuan reported the Shi brothers' conspiracy, and the emperor ordered their arrest.

sentences.zh: 祀時直在內殿，疑有異，遣信報祏曰：「劉暄似有異謀，今作何計？

translations.literal: Si was then on duty in the inner hall, suspected something unusual, and sent a messenger to report to Shi: "Liu Xuan seems to have some unusual plot—what shall we do now?
translations.idiomatic: Si was then on duty in the inner hall, sensed something amiss, and sent a messenger to Shi: "Liu Xuan seems to be plotting something—what should we do?

sentences.zh: 」祏曰：「政當靜以鎮之耳。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The proper course is simply to maintain calm composure."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "We should simply keep calm and hold steady."

sentences.zh: 」俄而召祏入見，停中書省。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Shi was summoned for an audience and detained at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Shi was summoned for an audience and detained at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，直齋袁文曠以王敬則勳當封，祏執不與。

translations.literal: Earlier, the direct-attendant guard Yuan Wenkuan, whose merit under Wang Jingze deserved enfeoffment, had been denied by Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the direct-attendant guard Yuan Wenkuan, whose service under Wang Jingze merited enfeoffment, had been denied his reward by Shi.

sentences.zh: 帝使文曠取祏，以刀環築其心曰：「復能奪我封否？

translations.literal: The emperor had Wenkuan seize Shi and beat his chest with the ring of a sword, saying: "Can you still deny me an enfeoffment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Wenkuan seize Shi and beat his chest with a sword hilt, saying, "Can you still deny me my enfeoffment?

sentences.zh: 」祏、祀同日見殺。

translations.literal: Shi and Si were killed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Si were executed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 祀字景昌，初爲南郡王國常侍，歷高祖驃騎東閤祭酒，祕書丞，晉安王鎮北長史，南東海太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: Si, courtesy name Jingchang, first served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Nanjun, then Eastern Pavilion libationer under the Taizu's Rapid Cavalry command, Secretary, northern-campaign senior clerk under the King of Jin'an, Administrator of Eastern Donghai, and acting prefectural and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Si, courtesy name Jingchang, first served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Nanjun, then Eastern Pavilion libationer under Emperor Gao's Rapid Cavalry command, Secretary, northern-campaign senior clerk under the King of Jin'an, Administrator of Eastern Donghai, and acting prefect of the commandery and province.

sentences.zh: 治下有宣尼廟，久廢不脩，祀更開掃構立。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction there was a Confucius temple long abandoned and unrepaired; Si reopened it, swept it clean, and rebuilt it.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction stood a Confucius temple long abandoned and unrepaired; Si reopened it, cleaned it, and rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 祀弟禧，居喪早卒。

translations.literal: Si's younger brother Xi died early while in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Si's younger brother Xi died young while in mourning.

sentences.zh: 有子廞，字偉卿，年十二，聞收至，謂家人曰：「伯旣如此，無心獨存。

translations.literal: He had a son Yin, courtesy name Weiqing, twelve years old; when he heard the arrest had come, he told his family: "Since my uncle is already in such straits, I have no heart to live alone.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yin, courtesy name Weiqing, twelve years old; when he heard that the arrest had come, he told his family, "Since my uncle is already in such straits, I have no wish to live on alone.

sentences.zh: 」赴井死。

translations.literal: He threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 後帝於後堂騎馬致適，顧謂左右曰：「江祏若在，我當復能騎此不？」

translations.literal: Later, as the emperor was riding a horse for pleasure in the rear hall, he looked back and said to those beside him: "If Jiang Shi were still alive, could I still ride this?
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the emperor was riding for pleasure in the rear hall, he turned to those beside him and said, "If Jiang Shi were still alive, would I still be able to ride like this?"

sentences.zh: 暄字士穆，出身南陽國常侍。

translations.literal: Xuan, courtesy name Shimu, entered service as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, courtesy name Shimu, began his career as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the State of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 遙光起事，以討暄爲名。

translations.literal: When Yaoguang raised the affair, he took punishing Xuan as his rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang launched his revolt, he took punishing Liu Xuan as his public justification.

sentences.zh: 事平，暄遷領軍將軍，封平都縣侯，千戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Xuan was transferred to General of the Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was suppressed, Xuan was made General of the Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其年，又見殺。

translations.literal: That same year he was again killed.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 和帝中興元年，贈祏衞將軍，暄散騎常侍、撫軍將軍，竝開府儀同三司，祀散騎常侍、太常卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Emperor He, Shi was posthumously given General of the Guard; Xuan irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army, both with offices equal to the Three Excellencies; Si irregular attendant-in-ordinary and Minister of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing under Emperor He, Shi was posthumously honored as General of the Guard; Xuan as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army, both with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies; and Si as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and Minister of Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：士死知己，蓋有生所共情，雖愚智之品有二，而逢迎之運唯一。

translations.literal: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is an emotion shared by all who live; though in wit and folly there are two grades, the fortune of winning favor is one alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is a feeling common to all who live; though wit and folly divide men into two kinds, the fortune of winning favor is singular.

sentences.zh: 夫懷可知之才，受知人之眄，無慚外物，此固天理，其猶藏在中心，銜恩念報。

translations.literal: When one harbors talent that can be known and receives the glance of one who knows men, without shame before outward things—this is indeed the way of heaven; it is as though stored within the heart, cherishing grace and thinking of repayment.
translations.idiomatic: When one possesses talent that can be recognized and receives the favor of one who knows men, unashamed before the world—this is the way of heaven itself, as though grace were stored in the heart and repayment always in mind.

sentences.zh: 況乎義早蕃僚，道同遇合，踰越勝己，顧邁先流，弃子如遺，曾微舊德，使狗之喻，人致前譏，慚包疚心，我無其事。

translations.literal: How much the more when they were bound early as feudal staff, united in the Way through mutual encounter, surpassing those better than themselves, looking back and exceeding those who came before, casting off sons as though forgotten, scarcely heeding old grace—the simile of the dog makes others bring forward reproof; burdened with shame and guilt in heart, I for my part have no such deed.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when men were joined early as feudal staff, united in purpose through mutual encounter, surpassing those above them and looking back beyond those who came before, casting off their sons as though they were nothing and scarcely remembering old kindness—the simile of the dog invites reproach from others; ashamed and guilty in heart, I for my part have no such deed.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 陸機所以賦豪士也。

translations.literal: This is why Lu Ji composed his rhapsody on the proud knight.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Lu Ji wrote his rhapsody on the proud knight.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王蕭提契，世祖基之。

translations.literal: In praise: Wang and Xiao raised the covenant; the late emperor founded upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Wang and Xiao raised the covenant, and Emperor Shizu built the foundation upon it.

sentences.zh: 樂羊食子，里克無辭。

translations.literal: Yue Yang ate his son; Li Ke had no words to say.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yang ate his son; Li Ke had nothing to say in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 江、劉后戚，明嗣是維。

translations.literal: Jiang and Liu, empress kin, upheld the Ming succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Liu clans, as empress kin, upheld the Ming succession.

sentences.zh: 廢興異論，終用乖疑。

translations.literal: Deposing and enthroning drew differing opinions; in the end suspicion prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing and enthroning provoked conflicting views, and in the end mutual suspicion carried the day.

translations.idiomatic: Footnote 1.
